title: Cross-Collateral Clause of the Equipment & Vehicle Loans Security Agreement
content:
**Clause.** Every Equipment & Vehicle Loans loan a member holds is secured by the units pledged to it and, under the cross-collateral clause of the security agreement, by the units pledged to the member's other equipment loans. A unit may be released on sale, substituted or released after total loss only when none of the member's other equipment loans is in nonaccrual status or has a past-due installment (the count of such other loans is 0). The same test applies to a deferral. Paying a loan off in full always releases that loan's own units, whatever the state of the member's other loans. The loan-to-value test after a release or substitution is applied to each loan on its own principal and its own remaining pledged value.

## Basis of the test

- **What is tested:** the member's other equipment loans — every equipment loan held under the same member, other than the loan whose unit is being released, substituted or whose installment is being deferred.
- **What each of them must show:** a status other than nonaccrual, and no installment past its due date unpaid.
- **Authority:** the loan records — each loan's status and its installment due dates as the system shows them before the action. A member's statement about the other loans does not take the place of the records.
- **Actions it governs:** a release on sale, a substitution, a release after total loss, and a deferral. A payoff in full is outside it: the paid-off loan's own units are released whatever the other loans show.

## Combinations

| Member's other equipment loans | Release on sale, substitution, total-loss release or deferral | Payoff release of the loan's own units |
|---|---|---|
| None in nonaccrual, none with a past-due installment | Test met | Released |
| At least one in nonaccrual status | Test not met | Released |
| At least one with a past-due installment | Test not met | Released |
| The member holds no other equipment loan | Test met (no other loan to fail it) | Released |

## Loan-to-value after a release or substitution

The loan-to-value test that follows a release or substitution looks at one loan at a time: that loan's own principal against that loan's own remaining pledged value. Units pledged to the member's other loans are not added to the value tested, even though the cross-collateral clause secures each loan by them.
